lead.t: *Broad complex ($\ge$0.12 s):* Ventricular tachycardia until proven otherwise; alternatively, SVT with aberrant conduction or pre-excitation (Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome).

snip.t: *Broad complex ($\ge$0.12 s):* Ventricular tachycardia until proven otherwise; alternatively, SVT with aberrant conduction or pre-excitation (Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome).
Adenosine: Contraindicated in asthma and severe reactive airway disease (can precipitate bronchospasm) and pre-excited AF (Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome).

MI, AF, 1st 2nd and 3rd degree heart block, p pulmonale, p mitrale, Wolff- Parkinson-White syndrome, LBBB, RBBB, Left and Right axis deviation, LVH, pericarditis, Hyper- and hypokalaemia, prolonged QT.
Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome can cause both Left and Right axis deviation

qs.q: An ECG of a child with Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome shows typical features when tachycardia subsides. Which of the following is characteristic of these baseline ECG findings?
o: Delta waves and short PR interval
Deep Q waves in the inferior leads
Narrow QRS complexes without any notching
qs.e: WPW syndrome is characterized by wide QRS complexes, delta waves, and a short PR interval when the tachycardia subsides. A prolonged PR interval would contradict the hallmark short PR interval caused by pre-excitation.
